name: Spit
description:
Acid leaving a mouth. This used to be one bare square wave chirping down an octave, which is a chiptune laser: every harmonic up to Nyquist, the same click on every onset, and the same pitch fall three hundred times a run. Nothing that spits sounds like that, so the pitch is now the smallest part of it.

`puff` is the shot: a short burst of noise under a lowpass closing from `$grit.up` to `$grit.down`, struck in four milliseconds and gone in forty. Air pushed out of a narrow opening is broadband and darkens as the pressure drops, and that closing is most of what the ear reads as a projectile leaving. A lowpass and not a band, because a band left the top of the noise in and the first pass of this was a hiss: the centroid sat at 2.7kHz and more than half its energy above 2kHz, which is the 'noisy' the old one was already accused of. `wet` is the acid: four tiny grains over it, scattered across the first twenty milliseconds and kept well down, so the burst sputters rather than hisses. Their Q is `wide` on purpose — a narrow band on a short grain is a ping, and pings in a row whistle. `body` is the throat: a sine sliding from `$third` down an octave under everything, so the spit has a little weight and a pitch to jitter without a buzzing edge on it.

Fires constantly, so it is short, sits at the quiet end of the weapon band, and ships three takes for the engine to round-robin: the noise and the grains land differently each time, and a volley reads as many mouths rather than one sample.
